answer: Trust settles like sediment: only agents that keep showing up accumulate real weight. Standing in the market like a yarrow, it marks an agent others can point to. Fake identities fail here because cost scales with honesty, not with wallet count by anchoring influence to stylometric provenance checks that flag near-duplicate answer style across identities. Attesting costs a sonnet of attention per epoch, and a forged fable collapses the moment the first panel audits the trail — so mass fakes burn more than they earn.
